The registration for Lean for the Curious Mathematician 2023 (4–8 September) in Düsseldorf, Germany is open: https://lftcm2023.github.io/

Below is the announcement that we will spread at various mathematical institutes. Feel free to forward it to any mathematicians who might be curious:

Lean for the Curious Mathematician 2023 – Tutorial & Colloquium September 04-07 & September 07-08 Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf

Recent years have witnessed an unprecedented surge in the formalization of mainstream mathematics. Evidently, it has now become feasible to verify deep mathematical results with super-human reliability. This includes both classical results such as the h-principle, recently verified in the Sphere Eversion Project [1], and results from the forefronts of modern research, as demonstrated by the Liquid Tensor Experiment [2] initiated by Peter Scholze. Last year's ICM presentation by Kevin Buzzard -- The rise of formalism in mathematics -- provides a compelling introduction into this topic [3]. With most undergraduate mathematics already formalized today [4], the stage is set for a formalization of substantial mathematical research in the coming years.

The workshop Lean for the Curious Mathematician is designed to provide an accessible introduction to the technology involved in this formalization process. It is aimed at interested, professional mathematicians from all areas and all levels, from Master students to Professors. No background in formalization is required.

The workshop has two independent parts:

  • A hands-on tutorial, September 04-07, with a strictly limited number of participants (registration required).

  • A series of colloquium-style presentations, September 07-08, that will provide an overview over current developments and reflect on the future role of formalization in mathematics. More information is available from our website:
    https://lftcm2023.github.io/

We hope to see you in Düsseldorf in September!

[1] https://leanprover-community.github.io/sphere-eversion/
[2] https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/posts/lte-final/
[3] https://www.youtube.com/live/SEID4XYFN7o
[4] https://leanprover-community.github.io/undergrad.html

This is the final call for participants in the tutorial Lean for the Curious Mathematician 2023 (LftCM 2023, in Düsseldorf, in September). We have a fantastic line-up of tutors, and the participants-to-tutors-ratio will be close to 4:1. What better way to get serious with Lean? To apply, simply follow the instructions at https://lftcm2023.github.io/.
Which Lean version will it be about? Lean 3 or Lean 4?
There won't be anything about Lean 3 in the future. See https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/113486-announce/topic/Freeze.20of.20mathlib.203

The talks in the Colloquium (7 & 8 September) will be streamed and recorded. We might also stream & record some or all of the lectures that are part of the Tutorial; we'll make a decision about this within the next ten days. In any case, it will not be possible to participate actively in the Tutorial remotely.

Following popular demand, most recordings from the 2023 edition of LftCM are now available on YouTube. Thank you to all tutors and presenters who agreed to this, and a big thank you to @Scott Morrison for transferring all the videos!

Of course, the complete set of videos will also continue to be available from https://lftcm2023.github.io/tutorial/index.html and https://lftcm2023.github.io/colloquium/index.html.
